svg.title: UsageTool settings — Providers, Menu Bar, and setup sheets
svg.desc: Native macOS 27 Settings window with toolbar tabs and grouped forms for configuring providers and menu-bar items, plus the two setup sheets.
svg.text: 1 · Settings › Providers — Codex, Claude adapter, OpenRouter management key

g.text: Reads the remaining subscription usage that the locally installed, signed-in Codex CLI reports
through its App Server. UsageTool never asks for an OpenAI account or API key.
A small adapter runs as Claude Code’s status line, keeps only the rate-limit fields, and writes
them to a snapshot file that UsageTool reads. No Claude sign-in or credentials are used.
Installed · composes with your existing status line
Last reported by Claude Code · 4m ago
Updates only while a Claude Code session is running.
Shows remaining USD account credits from OpenRouter’s credits API. Reading credits requires a
management key. UsageTool explains what that key can do before you add one.
Stored in the macOS Keychain and sent only to openrouter.ai.
This key can manage your OpenRouter API keys. Revoke it any time at

svg.text: 2 · Settings › Menu Bar — live preview, main item, separate text items, warnings

g.text: Show a text item for each provider. Each opens the same usage view beneath itself. Drag to reorder.

svg.text: 3 · Sheets — management-key disclosure (§7.7) and Configure Adapter (§7.5)

g.text: OpenRouter’s credits endpoint (/api/v1/credits) only accepts a management
key. OpenRouter doesn’t document a narrower, balance-only scope, so
A management key can create, edit and revoke your account’s API keys,
although it can’t make completion requests. UsageTool uses it for exactly
one thing: reading your credit balance.
Create the key with an expiry date. UsageTool stores it in the macOS
Keychain, sends it only to openrouter.ai, and will remind you a week before
it expires. Revoke it any time at openrouter.ai › Settings › Keys.
Set up the Claude Code status-line adapter
Claude Code runs a statusLine command and passes it status JSON on stdin. UsageTool’s
adapter keeps only the 5-hour and 7-day rate-limit windows (remaining, reset time)
and writes them to a snapshot file. Nothing else is stored, and no credentials are used.
Installs the adapter helper, backs up ~/.claude/settings.json, and merges only the
statusLine key. Your existing command keeps running inside --chain.
the adapter and written atomically. There is nothing to choose.
Data appears only after Claude Code’s first API response in a session and updates
only while a session is running. Between sessions the last report ages into Stale.
The adapter never reads or writes Claude credentials and never stores session IDs,
working directories, transcript paths, cost or context data.
